subject: Recap + proposed tail-latency A/B lab for Redwood vs CloudX
messages:
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: QA Team <qa@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — clarifying SLAs for tail latency

Thanks again for the demo today — that clarified a lot. A few concrete follow-ups from our side before we commit to the eval lab: 

- Our primary safety net is p99 under 2000ms for single-request flows at our typical windowed context (~1.2k tokens). If Redwood can show consistent p99 < 2s at our traffic shape, that's compelling.
- We want to run an A/B against CloudX’s managed inference (us-east) for: p95, p99, 50th, and tokens/sec.
- Can you provide a short test plan and what infra/config you’d use so our SREs can validate parity?

Attaching the demo logs we captured today (abbreviated). We'll also need an estimate for cost per 1M tokens for the proposed test duration.

Tom
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Attachment: acme-demo-logs-20280320.csv (csv, 42 KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — clarifying SLAs for tail latency

Tom — thanks for the clear targets and the logs. High level response and next steps below. I’m putting Ben (SE) and Aditya (solutions) on copy to scope the lab.

Summary (short):
- Redwood can run a focused tail-latency A/B against CloudX using your sample traffic shape. We aim to capture p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec and end-to-end latency including network hop when feasible.
- Proposed test days: 3 business days of steady-state runs + 1 day of stress/failure injection.
- Primary success criteria: p99 < 2s for 90% of runs, tokens/sec within 10% of CloudX baseline, and reproducible traces for any outliers.

What we need from Acme before we kickoff:
1) A redacted sample request set (you already sent an abbreviated logs file — ideal would be a 1k sample set).
2) Allowed test window and IP allowlist entries for any private endpoints.
3) Confirmation on whether the CloudX side will run with the same model version and max_context.

Ben — can you sketch a lab plan (baseline config, quantization/precision, batching, warm-up, measurement tooling)? Aditya — quick doc on cost estimate for the runs and the proposed rollback/fallback policy.

I'll prepare an engagement doc and share a short Drive link with the test plan and timeline. Proposed kickoff: Monday 26 Mar, unless you prefer earlier.

—Vanessa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-tail-latency-proposal-20280322.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — lab plan (technical scope)

Tom/Vanessa — putting the technical bones here so Acme's SRE/QA can review. I'll keep this high-level and attach the measurement checklist to the Drive doc.

Proposed Redwood lab configuration (baseline):
- Model: rwd-large-v2 (the same family we demoed). Fallback variant: rwd-large-quant8 for cost runs.
- Instance/infra: Dedicated GPU pool (g4dn.12x equivalent for parity), us-east.
- Precision: fp16 baseline, int8/quant variants for cost direction comparisons.
- Batching: request-level batching with adaptive batching window tuned to match your qps pattern (we'll share the batch-size distribution).
- Warm-up: 10k tokens warm-up per model variant to prime KV caches.
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end), tokens/sec, cold-start tail events, and memory pressure GC events.
- Failure injection: 10% network latency + 1% packet loss for one run day to validate graceful degradation/fallbacks.

Data collection and reproducibility:
- We'll produce per-request traces (timestamped) and an aggregated CSV matching the columns in your demo log.
- We'll tag runs with run-id and provide the run config JSON (model weights, kernel selection hints, quant flags).

Open questions for Acme:
- Do you want network-included latencies (client -> Redwood -> model) or strictly server-side? We can provide both but need to agree on clocks and trace correlation.
- Will CloudX be able to run the same exact model binary/version? If not, we'll note version differences in the results.

Expected timeline: draft lab plan by end of day Thu 22 Mar; kickoff and credentials exchange next week.

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
